title: Notes from E-Marking Centre on SSC-I Computer Science Examination April/May 2019
subject: Computer Science
introduction: This document has been produced for the teachers and candidates of Secondary School Certificate (SSC-I) Computer Science. It contains comments on candidates' responses to the 2019 SSC-I Examination, indicating the quality of the responses and highlighting their relative strengths and weaknesses, along with complete 2025 Syllabus SLO mappings and solved model answers.
generalObservations: In general, questions related to the types of programming translators (Q.1a), types of programming languages (Q.1b, Q.6a), input and output devices (Q.2b), number system conversions (Q.3), generations of computers (Q.6a), computer architecture (Q.6b), and MS Word (Q.4b) were well attempted.

Questions based on memory unit conversions (Q.2a), Windows BIOS installation (Q.4a), MS PowerPoint animation timing (Q.4c), DOS commands (Q.5b, Q.7b), and differentiation between Windows and DOS (Q.7a) required stronger conceptual practice.

questions.questionText: There is a set of video files in which the size of each file is 64 megabytes (MBs). How many of these video files can be stored in a flash drive with the storage capacity of 1 gigabyte (GB)? Show your working. (2 Marks)
questions.currentSloDescription: distinguish among the memory measuring units such as bits, bytes, kilobytes, megabytes, and gigabytes in computer memory;
questions.sloText: Distinguish among the memory measuring units such as bits, bytes, kilobytes, megabytes, and gigabytes in computer memory;
checkingHints: 1 mark for converting 1 GB = 1024 MB.
1 mark for dividing 1024 / 64 = 16 video files.
questions.overallPerformance: Questions based on memory unit conversions showed mixed performance where candidates forgot to convert GB to MB before dividing.
questions.betterResponses: Better responses converted gigabyte into megabytes (1 GB = 1024 MB) and applied division (1024 / 64 = 16 files) to get the required answer.
questions.weakerResponses: Weaker responses demonstrated poor conceptual knowledge about converting gigabytes into megabytes and multiplied 64 × 1024 = 65536 GB.
suggestions: Practise step-by-step unit conversion hierarchies (1 KB = 1024 B, 1 MB = 1024 KB, 1 GB = 1024 MB) before dividing storage capacities.
questions.modelAnswer:
### Part a: Number of 64 MB Video Files in a 1 GB Flash Drive (2 Marks)
1. Convert flash drive capacity from Gigabytes (GB) to Megabytes (MB):
   $$1\text{ GB} = 1024\text{ MB}$$
2. Divide total storage capacity by the size of each video file:
   $$\text{Number of files} = \frac{1024\text{ MB}}{64\text{ MB}} = 16\text{ files}$$
- Therefore, **16 video files** of 64 MB each can be stored in a 1 GB flash drive.

questions.modelAnswer:
### Part b: Input and Output Components of the Mobile Phone (3 Marks)
- **Two Input Components (2 Marks — 1 Mark Each):**
  1. **Keypad / Buttons:** Used by the user to dial phone numbers, type text messages (SMS), and navigate through menus.
  2. **Microphone (Mic):** Captures the user's spoken voice (sound waves) and converts it into electrical/digital audio signals during a phone call.
- **One Output Component (1 Mark):**
  1. **Display Screen / Monitor (LCD):** Visually displays the time, date, menus, contacts, and text messages to the user.
  2. *(Alternative valid output)* **Speaker / Earpiece:** Converts incoming electrical audio signals into audible sound so the user can hear the caller's voice or ringtones.

questions.questionText:
A computer controlled car is programmed in such a way that it moves in different directions on receiving specific binary codes (numbers).
The binary codes with corresponding directions are given below.

| Binary Code | Direction |
| :--- | :--- |
| `1010` | Forward |
| `0101` | Backward |
| `1101` | Left |
| `1011` | Right |

In order to move the car, the operator uses the given hexadecimal digits: **`5 B A D`**
Determine the direction in which the car will move for each hexadecimal digit. *(Note: Show your working.)* (4 Marks)
questions.sloText: Convert hexadecimal numbers into binary numbers and vice versa (Legacy Topic 5: Number Systems);
checkingHints: 1 mark for each correct hexadecimal-to-binary conversion and direction: 5 = 0101 (Backward), B = 1011 (Right), A = 1010 (Forward), D = 1101 (Left).
questions.overallPerformance: Well attempted by candidates who knew hexadecimal digit values A=10, B=11, D=13.
questions.betterResponses: Better responses converted the hexadecimal numbers into 4-bit binary numbers and mapped each binary number against the directions given in the table.
questions.weakerResponses: Weaker responses determined the direction for digit 5 but failed to convert the alphabetical hexadecimal digits A, B, and D.
suggestions: Reinforce hexadecimal alphabetical digit values (A=10, B=11, C=12, D=13, E=14, F=15) and 4-bit binary conversion.
questions.modelAnswer:
### Step 1: Convert Each Hexadecimal Digit to 4-Bit Binary (Working)
- **Hexadecimal `5`** $= 5_{10} = (0101)_2 \rightarrow$ matches **`Backward`**
- **Hexadecimal `B`** $= 11_{10} = 8 + 2 + 1 = (1011)_2 \rightarrow$ matches **`Right`**
- **Hexadecimal `A`** $= 10_{10} = 8 + 2 = (1010)_2 \rightarrow$ matches **`Forward`**
- **Hexadecimal `D`** $= 13_{10} = 8 + 4 + 1 = (1101)_2 \rightarrow$ matches **`Left`**

### Step 2: Completed Direction Table

| Hexadecimal Digit | 4-Bit Binary Equivalent | Direction |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **`5`** | `0101` | **Backward** |
| **`B`** | `1011` | **Right** |
| **`A`** | `1010` | **Forward** |
| **`D`** | `1101` | **Left** |

### Part a: Purpose of Utility Software and User Interface (2 Marks)
- **i. Utility Software (1 Mark):** System software designed to **analyse, configure, optimise, maintain, and protect** a computer system and its operating system (for example, antivirus scanners, disk defragmenters, backup utilities, and file compression tools).
- **ii. User Interface (1 Mark):** The visual or text-based bridge/medium through which a **user interacts and communicates with the computer system** and operating system (e.g., Command Line Interface [CLI] or Graphical User Interface [GUI]).

questions.currentSloDescription: explain the following types of system software: a. operating system, b. device drivers, c. utility programs, d. language processors;

questions.overallPerformance: Slightly higher number of candidates attempted Part (a) and performed moderately well.

questions.modelAnswer:
### Part a: Windows OS (GUI) vs MS-DOS (CLI) (8 Marks)
**i. FOUR Advantages of Windows Operating System over DOS (4 Marks — 1 Mark Each):**
1. **Intuitive Graphical User Interface (GUI):** Windows uses visual icons, menus, windows, and a mouse pointer (`WIMP`), so users do not need to memorise complex text commands as in DOS.
2. **Multitasking & Multi-User Support:** Windows can run multiple applications simultaneously in separate windows, whereas DOS is a single-user, single-tasking system.
3. **Plug and Play (PnP) Hardware Support:** Windows automatically detects and configures newly connected hardware peripherals, whereas DOS requires manual driver configuration.
4. **Rich Multimedia & Networking Support:** Windows natively supports high-resolution graphics, audio/video playback, drag-and-drop file sharing, and modern networking.

**ii. FOUR Disadvantages of Windows Operating System over DOS (4 Marks — 1 Mark Each):**
1. **Higher Hardware & Memory Requirements:** Windows requires gigabytes of RAM, fast multi-core processors, and tens of gigabytes of disk space, whereas DOS runs in a few megabytes.
2. **Higher Licensing Cost:** Commercial Windows licences are more expensive than lightweight command-line systems.
3. **Greater Vulnerability to Malware/Viruses:** Due to its widespread use and background network services, Windows is targeted far more frequently by viruses and malware.
4. **Longer Installation & Boot Time / Slower Scripting:** Installing and booting full graphical Windows takes longer than booting a minimal DOS prompt.
